deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is working in a von Neumann algebra 𝒜 on ℋ with a faithful normal semifinite trace T. From the previous pages, μ_A, φ_A, … are the spectral distribution and decreasing-rearrangement functions of A. 𝔟 is an ideal of operators that are 'small' with respect to T, roughly with support of finite trace or τ-compact. a is the trace-class ideal L¹(𝒜,T). On the previous page (§6) he defines a determinant Δ(A) = exp ∫_0^{T(1)} log φ_{|A|}(t) dt. When T is finite this is exactly the Fuglede–Kadison determinant (Annals 1952). This page continues case (b), T infinite, with A ≥ 0 written as A = λ1 + B, B ∈ 𝔟. Then φ_{|A|}(t) → λ as t → ∞, which gives three cases. (a) If |λ| < 1, the integral of log diverges to −∞, so Δ(A) = 0. (b) If |λ| > 1, Δ(A) = +∞. (c) If |λ| = 1, 0 ≤ Δ(A) ≤ +∞, and Δ(A) < +∞ iff B ∈ a. Hence 0 ≤ Δ(1+A) < +∞ for A ∈ a, so the natural domain of the determinant in the semifinite case is the affine set 1 + a (1 + trace class). A crossed-out passage mentions continuity of Δ on 1 + a. Prop 8 states that on 1 + a: Δ(A) = Δ(A*), Δ(AB) = Δ(A)Δ(B), Δ(1) = 1. This is a multiplicative determinant on the group-like set 1 + L¹ of a semifinite algebra, i.e. a Fredholm-determinant analogue in the type II_∞ / type I_∞ setting. Proof strategy, begun here and carried on the next page: let ε(A) be the projection onto the closure of Aℋ (range projection; ε(A) ∈ 𝒜). For a projection E, the corner 𝒜_E = E𝒜E is a von Neumann algebra on Eℋ with induced trace T_E. Formula (5)/(3): Δ(1+A) = Δ_E(1_E + A_E) whenever A ∈ 𝒜_E. For E of finite trace this reduces the semifinite determinant to the finite Fuglede–Kadison determinant in a finite corner. Then by a continuity/density argument one may assume A, B lie in a common finite corner 𝒜_E, where multiplicativity is Fuglede–Kadison's theorem. The next page shows crossed-out attempts to prove multiplicativity directly via Δ(AB)² = Δ(B*A*AB).
errors: The equivalence 'Δ(A) < +∞ ⟺ B ∈ a' in case |λ| = 1 is imprecise. If B is self-adjoint with B ≥ −1, its positive part not trace class forces +∞. But if only its negative part fails to be trace class, the log-integral tends to −∞ and Δ = 0 < ∞ with B ∉ a. Mixed cases give an ∞ − ∞ ambiguity that the integral definition with φ_{|A|} does not resolve without convention. The precise statement should be about the positive part, or require ∫ |log φ| < ∞.
Formula (5) requires A ∈ 𝒜_E (e.g. E ≥ ε(A) ∨ ε(A*)), not only E = ε(A). The next page corrects this to 'si A ∈ 𝒜_E'.

The reduction in Prop 8 to a common finite corner by continuity needs continuity of Δ on 1 + a in the L¹-norm. This is plausible but nontrivial: Δ is not continuous at non-invertible points. The relevant remarks are crossed out, so the gap is not closed on this page.

ideas.what: Fuglede–Kadison determinant via exp ∫ log of the decreasing rearrangement of |A|
ideas.where_published: possibly alluded to in Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955) on rearrangements in von Neumann algebras; unsure

ideas.what: Extension to semifinite (infinite trace) algebras: trichotomy for λ1 + B, and natural domain 1 + L¹ where Δ is finite
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison / Fredholm determinant on 1 + L¹(M,τ) in semifinite von Neumann algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: L.G. Brown (Lidskii theorem in type II case, 1986); de la Harpe–Skandalis (1984) for the trace-determinant formalism

ideas.what: Multiplicativity Δ(AB) = Δ(A)Δ(B), Δ(A*) = Δ(A) on 1 + a
Reduction to corner algebras E𝒜E with induced trace, Δ(1+A) = Δ_E(1_E + A)

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck sets up a determinant theory for semifinite von Neumann algebras. He identifies 1 + (trace class) as the natural domain, gives the trichotomy 0 / +∞ / finite according to |λ|, and states multiplicativity there. This anticipates the semifinite Fuglede–Kadison/Fredholm determinant usually attributed to work of the 1980s (L.G. Brown; de la Harpe–Skandalis).
missed.quote: On a donc, 0≤Δ(1+A)<+∞ si A∈a … Prop 8 Δ(A)=Δ(A*), Δ(AB)=Δ(A)Δ(B), Δ(1)=1, A,B ∈ 1+a
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority point in the history of determinants in operator algebras. Semifinite Fuglede–Kadison determinants are used in L²-invariants, the Brown measure and Lidskii-type theorems.

missed.claim: The proof of multiplicativity is only sketched: corner reduction plus an unproved continuity of Δ on 1 + a. The direct approach on the next page is abandoned.
missed.quote: Par ... de continuité, on peut supposer qu'il existe E … A∈𝒜_E, B∈𝒜_E
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The result is now known, but the continuity question for Δ on 1 + L¹ is delicate at non-invertible elements.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1953), apparently unpublished extension of the Fuglede–Kadison determinant to semifinite algebras on 1 + L¹, with multiplicativity. It predates the standard references by about 30 years. However, it is a natural extension, and the proof is incomplete on this page.
